zh.title: 可見 vs 黑盒
zh.question: 可見議會和原生黑盒，差別在過程還是在結論？跳過的席能不能寫進終稿。

analyst.answer: 差別在過程能不能被核對，不在結論好不好聽。
analyst.review: 看得到不等於每一步都真。回放仍要標明是策展。
brief: 可見和原生不是兩種聰明程度。可見模式把席位、跳過、互怼、引用都留在事件流裡，讀者可以對著結論往回核。原生模式只交一段終稿，過程在供應商那邊，我們看不到誰說了哪一句。好不好聽不能代替能不能核對。
沒出場的席不能在結論裡被補成好像說過話。門控跳過情報和文案，是因為這一題沒有可核對的外部來源，也沒有需要改寫的句子。把空白讀成沉默的同意，是議長最容易犯的錯，也是這一題要擋住的錯。
所以差別要寫在過程上，不寫在口味上。要展示就走可見，要省過程就標黑盒。標了黑盒，就不能再用「八席討論過」這種可見模式才配得上的句子。
可見不是更聰明，黑盒不是更差。我拒絕的是用同一個「八席討論過」去賣兩種買不到同一樣東西的模式。買到事件，才能核對。沒買到事件，就標黑盒。標了還寫八席，是把沒有的過程賣出去。

researcher.skip: 沒有可核對的外部來源，這一題不喚醒。

engineer.answer: 可見模式給席位事件。原生模式只給一段終稿。
engineer.review: 多出來的是事件，不是自動更準。
brief: 可見模式的產物是一串席位事件：誰醒了、誰被跳過、誰寫了立場、誰打了哪一句、議長引用了誰。這些事件可以回放，也可以被第三個人核對。沒有事件的句子，就不該被寫成某一席說過。
原生模式只給一段終稿。終稿可以很完整，但它沒有席位邊界。你無法指出哪一句是工程、哪一句是批評、哪一句是模型在終稿裡新補的。完整和可核對不是同一個性質。
所以介面不該用同一套「八席已討論」的裝飾去包兩種模式。可見就給席位事件。黑盒就標黑盒。裝飾相同，讀者會把不能核對的終稿讀成已經核對過。
沒有事件的句子，不進席位歸因。終稿可以很長，長不是席位邊界。我要的產物是一串能回放的事件，不是一段看起來分過席的散文。散文分席，是裝飾。事件分席，才是可見模式真正交出的東西。

critic.answer: 沒出場的席，不能在結論裡被補成好像說過話。
critic.review: 省 Token 可以。假裝全席說過話，不行。
brief: 我要打的是補寫，不是文風。這一題情報和文案被門控跳過。如果結論寫「情報員也認為」，那就是議長在替沒出場的席說話。沒出場的席沒有立場，空白不是同意，也不是反對。
可見模式的價值就在這一句可以被抓住。事件流裡沒有那一席，引用就不成立。原生模式做了同樣的補寫，讀者看不出來。看不出來不是更安全，是更難追。
所以批評席不評價終稿好不好聽。我只問：結論裡的每個主語，事件流裡有沒有對應的一句。沒有，就刪主語，不要為了對稱把八個名字排齊。
這一題我只抓補寫。情報和文案沒出場，結論裡出現他們的動詞，就是議長在替他們說話。動詞包括同意、反對、確認、補充。空白沒有動詞。誰替空白填了動詞，誰越界。

strategist.answer: 要展示就走可見。要省過程就標黑盒。
strategist.review: 核對的是事件，不是語氣。
brief: 選擇先看你要對誰負責。要給讀者核對，就走可見，接受事件更貴、過程更吵。要省過程，就標黑盒，接受你不能把終稿說成八席共識。兩個目標都合理，混在一個標籤裡不合理。
黑盒不是失敗。失敗是用黑盒的成本，賣可見的可信。省掉了事件，又在文案裡寫「席位互相審查過」，讀者買到的是一個無法兌現的句子。
推薦寫在選擇條件上，不寫成口味。展示給人看，用可見。只需要一段答案，用黑盒，並且把黑盒寫在答案旁邊。不要把兩種模式的優點加在同一句話裡。
兩個目標都寫在選擇上，不寫成口味。給人核對，付事件的錢。省過程，標黑盒，並停用可見模式才配的句子。不要承諾一個你沒有留下證據的共識。沒有證據的共識，比沒有共識更貴，因為它會被引用。

writer.skip: 這一題比的是過程，不需要另一套文案。

quant.answer: 可見更貴在事件，不自動更準。
quant.review: 別把延遲差寫成品質差。
brief: 可見更貴，貴在事件，不自動更準。每一條席位事件都是 token，八席全醒比一段終稿貴。貴不證明結論更好，便宜也不證明結論更差。準確要另測，不能從帳單反推。
所以不要把「更貴」寫成「更可信」的證據。可信來自能核對：跳過有記錄、引用有原文、互怼打在具體的句子上。這些是事件的性質，不是單價。
如果只為了省，就走黑盒，並在帳上記「少了過程」。如果要核對，就付事件的錢。兩筆不要加成一個「划算」，因為你省下的和你失去的不在同一列。
貴和準分列。可見的額外成本是事件條數乘 token，不是一個可信度係數。我不會簽「更貴所以更對」。要證明更對，另測。帳單只證明你買了過程，不證明過程得出了更好的終稿。

chair.answer: 可見與黑盒的差別是過程能不能核對。沒出場的席，不能寫進結論。
brief: 可見與黑盒的差別是過程能不能核對，不是終稿好不好聽。可見留下席位事件。黑盒只留下一段話。這一句是各席都站得住的，沒有人主張黑盒自動更準，也沒有人主張可見自動更便宜。
這一題情報和文案沒出場。結論不能寫他們同意，也不能寫他們反對。空白就是沒說話。把沒說話的席補成共識的一部分，是這一題明確要拒絕的寫法。
要展示就走可見，並接受事件更貴。要省過程就標黑盒，並停止使用「八席討論過」。貴和準分開記。沒出場的名字不進結論。
收場三條：過程能不能核對是唯一差別；沒出場的席不進結論；貴和準分開記。不寫八席討論過，除非八席都在事件流裡留下了句子。這一題沒有。所以不寫。

en.title: Visible vs black box
en.question: Is the difference the process or the verdict, and can a skipped seat enter the final draft?

analyst.answer: The difference is whether the process can be checked.
analyst.review: Visible is not the same as true. A replay must say it is curated.
brief: Visible and native are not two grades of intelligence. Visible keeps seats, skips, critiques, and citations in an event stream a reader can check against the verdict. Native returns one final text. The process stays with the vendor. We cannot see who said which sentence. A pleasant ending is not a checkable one.

A seat that never appeared cannot be written into the verdict as if it had spoken. The gate skipped research and writing because this question has no external source to check and no sentence that needs rewriting. Reading a blank as silent agreement is the chair's easiest mistake, and the one this question is meant to stop.

So the difference belongs on the process, not on taste. If you want to show the work, use visible. If you want to skip the process, label the box. Once it is labeled a black box, you may not use a sentence that only the visible mode has earned, such as 'eight seats discussed it'.

Visible is not smarter, and a black box is not worse. What I refuse is selling both modes with the same 'eight seats discussed this', when the two purchases do not buy the same thing. You can check what you bought only if you bought events. If you did not, label the box. Writing eight seats after that label sells a process you do not have.

researcher.skip: No checkable outside source, so this seat stays out.

engineer.answer: Visible mode emits seat events. Native mode returns one draft.
engineer.review: You gain events, not automatic accuracy.
brief: What visible mode produces is a stream of seat events: who woke, who was skipped, who wrote a position, who struck which sentence, whom the chair cited. Those events can be replayed and checked by a third person. A sentence with no event should not be attributed to a seat.

Native mode returns one final text. The text can be complete and still have no seat boundary. You cannot point to which sentence was engineering, which was criticism, and which the model added while closing. Completeness and auditability are different properties.

The interface should not wrap both modes in the same 'eight seats discussed this' decoration. Visible gets seat events. A black box gets a black-box label. Identical decoration teaches the reader to treat an unchecked final text as already checked.

A sentence with no event does not get a seat attribution. A final text can be long. Length is not a seat boundary. The artifact I want is a stream that can be replayed, not prose that looks divided into seats. Dividing prose into seats is decoration. Dividing events into seats is what visible mode actually delivers.

critic.answer: A seat you did not see must not be written into the verdict.
critic.review: Saving tokens is fine. Pretending the full table spoke is not.
brief: The strike is about invention, not style. Research and writing were gated off for this question. If the verdict says 'the researcher also holds', the chair is speaking for a seat that never appeared. An absent seat has no position. A blank is not agreement and not dissent.

The point of visible mode is that this sentence can be caught. If the stream has no such seat, the citation fails. Native mode can invent the same line and the reader cannot see it. Invisible is not safer. It is harder to chase.
This seat does not grade how the final text sounds. It asks whether every subject in the verdict has a sentence in the stream. If not, drop the subject. Do not line up eight names for symmetry.

On this question I only catch invention. Research and writing did not appear. If the verdict gives them a verb, the chair is speaking for them. The verbs include agree, dissent, confirm, and add. A blank has no verb. Whoever supplies a verb for a blank has crossed the line.

strategist.answer: Show the process, or label the black box. Don't mix them.
strategist.review: Check the events, not the tone.
brief: Choose by who you have to answer to. If the reader must check, use visible, and accept that events cost more and the process is noisier. If you want to skip the process, label the black box, and accept that you cannot call the final text an eight-seat consensus. Both aims are reasonable. Mixing them in one label is not.

A black box is not a failure. The failure is selling visible trust at black-box cost. You skipped the events and still wrote that seats reviewed each other. The reader bought a sentence you cannot redeem.

Put the recommendation on the condition, not on taste. Showing the work means visible. Needing one answer means a black box, with the label beside the answer. Do not add the advantages of both modes into one sentence.

Both aims stay on the choice, not on taste. If someone must check, pay for events. If you skip the process, label the box and stop using sentences only visible mode has earned. Do not promise a consensus you left no evidence for. A consensus with no evidence costs more than no consensus, because it will be cited.

writer.skip: This topic is about the process, not a second wording.

quant.answer: Visible costs more events. It is not automatically more accurate.
quant.review: Don't write a latency gap as a quality gap.
brief: Visible costs more, and the extra cost is events, not automatic accuracy. Every seat event is tokens. Eight waking seats cost more than one final text. Expensive does not prove the conclusion is better. Cheap does not prove it is worse. Accuracy has to be measured separately. It cannot be inferred from the bill.

Do not use 'cost more' as evidence of 'more trustworthy'. Trust here means checkable: skips are recorded, citations have a source sentence, and a critique lands on a specific line. Those are properties of the events, not of the unit price.

If the only goal is to spend less, use the black box and write down that the process is missing. If the goal is a check, pay for the events. Do not add the two into 'a bargain'. What you saved and what you lost are not in the same column.

Cost and accuracy stay in separate columns. The extra cost of visible mode is event count times tokens, not a trust coefficient. I will not sign 'more expensive, therefore more correct'. Prove more correct separately. The bill only proves you bought a process. It does not prove the process produced a better final text.

chair.answer: The difference is whether the process can be checked. A seat that did not appear cannot enter the verdict.
brief: The difference between visible and black box is whether the process can be checked, not whether the final text sounds better. Visible leaves seat events. A black box leaves a paragraph. No seat claimed the black box is automatically more accurate, or that visible is automatically cheaper.

Research and writing did not appear on this question. The verdict cannot say they agreed, and it cannot say they dissented. A blank is silence. Writing a silent seat into the consensus is the move this question refuses.

Show the work and pay for events, or skip the process and label the box. Stop using 'eight seats discussed this' once the box is black. Cost and accuracy stay in separate columns. Names that never appeared do not enter the verdict.

Three lines at the close: whether the process can be checked is the only difference; a seat that did not appear does not enter the verdict; cost and accuracy are recorded apart. Do not write that eight seats discussed it unless eight seats left a sentence in the stream. They did not. So it is not written.
